references.text: God commands that all firstborns be consecrated to Him, which forms the basis for the Levites later being taken as a substitute for the firstborn.
The law concerning the firstborn belonging to the Lord, including the redemption of the firstborn, which the Levites now replace.
Reiterates the principle that the Levites are to be taken in place of all the firstborn among the children of Israel.
Confirmation that the Levites shall belong to the Lord, taken in place of the firstborn.
Explains that the Levites are given to the Lord from the children of Israel as a substitute for all the firstborn.
The Levites are set apart from Israel and given as a gift to the Lord for service in the tabernacle.
The firstborn of sons shall be given to the Lord, a principle upon which the selection of the Levites is based.
Refers to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, a spiritual parallel to the consecration of the firstborn.
Refers to the law that every male firstborn shall be called holy to the Lord.
